title: Multivariate uplift experimentation for batching/caching: metrics, analysis, and dashboards
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Design and run a multivariate A/B experiment framework to safely evaluate batching and prefix/KV caching config proposals. This ticket covers metric definitions, analysis approach (incl. uplift estimation and sequential stopping), visualization/dashboard spec, and automation hooks for safe apply + rollback. Goal: surface statistically and economically defensible recommendations for batching/caching profiles while protecting latency SLAs and quality budgets.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment test harness deployed to staging and can replay production slices
Instrumentation emits cohort-tagged telemetry for every request (batch size, cache_hit, config_id, token_count, latency_ms, quality_signal)
Analysis notebook demonstrates uplift estimates with credible intervals for cost and quality across cohorts
Dashboard with the panels described below is live in Grafana and linked in the ticket
Automation path documented: canary -> monitored apply -> automatic rollback when one or more rollback triggers fire
tasks: Finalize metric definitions and wire into telemetry (SLOs and economic metrics)
Implement test harness: shadow and split traffic runner with per-cohort tagging
Build sequential analysis pipeline: Bayesian uplift model + alpha spending schedule
Create Grafana dashboard and alerts + cost-savings heatmap
Run smoke experiments on synthetic workload and iterate thresholds
Document rollout/rollback automation and do tabletop runbook
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting with product and reliability. Agreed on primary goals: reduce per-token unit cost without increasing p95 latency above SLA or quality regressions > 1% ARR.

2026-03-11: Instrumentation PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/412). Added fields: experiment_id, cohort_id, config_hash, effective_batch_size, cache_hit, tokens_out, upstream_errors.

2026-03-12: Prototype Bayesian model completed in notebook and validated on replayed traffic from last 7 days. Initial uplift estimates show cost reduction signal with high uncertainty for low-volume cohorts.
analysis_plan: Primary objectives: estimate per-cohort net unit cost delta and Acceptable Response Rate (ARR) delta relative to baseline
Model: hierarchical Bayesian uplift model to borrow strength across small cohorts and produce posterior distributions for cost and quality deltas
Sequential testing: use Bayesian credible intervals with an alpha-spending schedule to allow early stopping for strong wins/losses while controlling overall false discovery
Heterogeneous effects: report cohort-level lift, and aggregate by traffic slice (region, model_size, route_type)
Economic decision: compute expected regret and expected savings per hour given current traffic mix; use decision threshold that factors in cost of rollback and operational risk
metrics_to_track: net_token_cost_per_request: USD per request after batching and caching
effective_batch_size_distribution: histogram of batch sizes produced by runtime
kv_cache_hit_rate: percent requests with prefix/KV cache hit
avg_tokens_saved_from_cache: tokens avoided due to cache hits
error_rate: upstream and runtime errors per 1k req
Acceptable Response Rate (ARR): proportion of responses passing quality checks (syntactic + prompt-specific heuristics)
model_quality_delta: automated eval metric (BLEU/ROUGE/perplexity) where applicable
dashboard_panels: Cost vs Quality scatter: x=net_token_cost_per_request, y=ARR delta with posterior intervals per cohort
Batch size heatmap: hour-of-day vs observed batch size distribution
Cache effectiveness: kv_cache_hit_rate + tokens_saved stacked area chart
Latency SLOs: p50/p95 lines with SLA bands and cohort breakdown
Sequential evidence plot: posterior mean and 95% credible band over time for cost and ARR; stop thresholds annotated
Expected savings curve: cumulative expected USD saved vs time for each config
Risk budget gauge: current probability of ARR degradation > threshold and remaining operational risk budget
Cohort uplift table: cohort_id, traffic_pct, cost_lift (mean ± CI), ARR_lift (mean ± CI), recommended_action
rollout_strategy: Stage 0 (Dry-run): run config in shadow mode for 24h on >10% mirrored traffic. Verify instrumentation and basic signals.
Stage 1 (Canary): apply to 5% of live traffic across representative cohorts for 48h with close monitoring.
Stage 2 (Adaptive ramp): increase allocation using Thompson-sampling-inspired adaptive allocation that favors higher expected savings but respects risk caps
Stage 3 (Full apply): apply globally when posterior probability of no-quality-regression > 97% and expected hourly savings > configured min_savings
All stages include preflight simulation using traffic replayer and require passing smoke checks before proceeding
rollback_triggers: ARR delta drop greater than 1.0% for 15 consecutive minutes in any high-volume cohort
p95 latency increase > 25% from baseline for more than 10 minutes
error_rate spike > 5x baseline OR absolute errors > 50/hr
unexpected drop in kv_cache_hit_rate > 20% compared to shadow baseline
automation: if Bayesian posterior probability that cost savings < 0.0 exceeds 90%
telemetry_events: experiment_start: emit when config is first scheduled for a request
cache_sample: emit per-request cache decision and matched prefix keys count
batch_flush: emitted when a batch is flushed with size and latency breakdown
quality_signal: result of automated quality check pipeline (pass/fail and reason)
rollback_executed: include trigger_reason and snapshot of last 10 minutes of metrics
